q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of an LPG gas stove?
title: Gas stove carbon footprint per unit
short: Weigh the stainless steel or toughened glass top, brass or aluminium burners, valves and pipes, and multiply each by its supplier's figure. Add pressing, assembly and leak testing energy per unit and packing. Metals are usually most of the total.

ul: Stainless or mild steel body and top, or toughened glass.
Brass or aluminium burners and caps.
Gas valves, knobs, nozzles and pan supports.
Sheet pressing, bending and spot welding.

p: Report per stove by burner count, since a four-burner model carries more metal than a two-burner.

example.title: Worked example: stove unit per piece (one month)
lines: LPG for testing: 500 kg x 2.98 = 1,490 kg CO2
Plant total: 19,240 / 20,000 = 0.962 kg CO2 per stove
Add steel, glass and brass for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
